items.title: Approval-to-compile launch is explicitly idempotent
items.statement: The page consumes the Planning Wizard approval transaction, binds a pending shell to the approval command and idempotency key, and forbids a duplicate compile launch during publication lag.
items.impact: A delayed PlanApproved projection does not create two PlanCompileRuns or misleading parallel launches.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator Plan Compile consumes the Planning Wizard `Approve And Build` approval transaction; it does not create a second ordinary build launch. When `cmd.planning_wizard.approve_and_build` succeeds locally, Orchestrator opens `Plan Compile` with either the returned durable `plan_compile_run_id` or a pending-launch projection tied to the approval command and idempotency key. If `PlanApproved` publication or projection reconciliation lags, the tab displays pending-launch status and then binds to the durable `PlanCompileRun` without creating a duplicate.

items.title: Blocked-owner vocabulary contradicts its exact eight-kind taxonomy
items.statement: One owner section names Run, Concern, Source Control, GitHub, Auth, Usage pressure, Wizard, and Recovery as blocked-owner examples, while the same document later says the kinds are exactly Runtime, Package Overseer, Seam Overseer, Corroboration, Graph Patch, Recovery, User, and External Resource. No alias-to-canonical mapping is supplied.
items.impact: Storage enums, filters, badges, and escalation routing can encode incompatible owner values and lose deterministic rendering.

evidence.exact_quote: Blocked-owner summaries identify the primary blocked owner or attention owner instead of only saying blocked; canonical examples include Run, Concern, Source Control, GitHub, Auth, Usage pressure, Wizard, and Recovery.
- Blocked-owner kinds are exactly `Runtime`, `Package Overseer`, `Seam Overseer`, `Corroboration`, `Graph Patch`, `Recovery`, `User`, and `External Resource`.

items.title: Concern merge and update behavior has no race-safe identity rule
items.statement: Workers nominate concerns and repeated sightings may update or mint records, but the specification gives no dedupe key, revision/CAS field, idempotency token, or deterministic winner for simultaneous sightings and owner reassignment.
items.impact: Concurrent emitters can create duplicate canonical concerns, overwrite a newer lifecycle state, or attach evidence to the wrong lineage.

evidence.exact_quote: Concern is a high-level first-class Orchestrator object. The lifecycle includes active, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed; runtime, package overseer, seam overseer, corroboration outcome, and graph patch logic may create canonical concerns, while workers nominate concerns rather than minting canonical concern records directly.
- Repeated sightings use source/scope/category/lineage-aware heuristics to decide whether to update an existing concern or mint a new concern record.

items.title: Self-initiated web evidence lacks untrusted-input and data-egress rules
items.statement: Permission and capability gates are named, but the web-operation contract does not constrain schemes, destinations, redirects, private-network targets, prompt-injected instructions, credential forwarding, captured-page secrets, or evidence-retention/redaction.
items.impact: Goal-driven fetch/crawl/browser work could become an SSRF, secret-exfiltration, or prompt-injection path while still producing apparently valid receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: - Orchestrator may self-initiate read-only web/search/fetch/extract/research/deep-research/crawl/map work only when orchestration needs current or external source verification, issue/PR/docs currentness, or visual/dynamic browser evidence. These calls route through the PM WebOperation/BrowserAction dispatcher, not through slash-help-only command discovery, and use `websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `webcrawl`, `webmap`, or `BrowserAction/Site Reader` with `invocation_source = goal`, required `agent_reason`, permission/capability gates, visible operation cards, and `orchestrator_evidence_receipts`. Orchestrator web evidence does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, runtime queues, implementation files, or build tasks; it records source/evidence receipts for the current GoalRun or blocked-state decision.

items.title: Cross-tab scale requirements are not measurable
items.statement: The document mandates slicing, virtualization, lazy expansion, and demand loading but defines no supported row/node counts, frame or interaction budget, page size, backpressure behavior, stable selection under eviction, or degraded threshold.
items.impact: Implementations can satisfy the named techniques while remaining unusable or inconsistent at realistic project scale.

evidence.exact_quote:
- Slice-based loading, virtualization, lazy expansion, and demand-loaded inspectors are mandatory across dense tabs.
- Scale is a cross-tab contract rather than a graph-tab-only concern.

items.title: Offline degradation and cancel-complete races are explicitly represented
items.statement: The source keeps safe local capability available during remote outages, records indeterminate outcomes, and reconciles cancel-versus-complete races to informational terminal states rather than overwriting success as failure.
items.impact: The GUI can preserve truthful local/remote state and avoid false failure states during late remote reconciliation.

evidence.exact_quote: - External side-effect receipts distinguish local-vs-remote and vs-remote outcomes. `indeterminate_remote_outcome` records `requested`, `transport_lost`, and later `reconciled` state plus a `Refresh remote state` CTA. Capability-level degradation and the local-vs-remote degraded-mode split keep local work available where safe: local Git can continue during hosted-degraded GitHub state, Docker local runtime can continue during registry outage, and manifest editing can continue while cluster access is offline.

- Terminal-state precedence rules for cancel/complete races are explicit; examples: cancel requested after a remote run already completed, container stop requested after the container already exited or restarted, and rollout cancel requested after a new revision already became ready. The receipt reconciles to an informational terminal state such as `completed_before_cancel`, `already_stopped`, or `already_replaced` instead of overwriting the completed outcome as failed.

items.title: Page, runtime, and user-action authority are deliberately separated
items.statement: OP-002 confines the page to presentation and intents, while OP-005 narrows user actions and keeps true HITL decisions distinct from generic runtime operations.
items.impact: The GUI cannot legitimately become scheduler truth merely because it exposes controls and projections.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator owns scheduling, concern tracking, blocked-state handling, runtime identity presentation, page layout and controls, view-model projections, and run-control intents for the Progress, Plan Compile, Seams, Node Graph, Evidence, History, and Ledger tab set, while runtime, storage, and scheduler contracts own canonical truth.
Concern actions expose authority, confirmation level, rationale requirements, reversibility, audit fields, compact inspectors, route-open full records, and narrow user-facing affordances.

items.title: Shared record envelope has no buildable common-field schema
items.statement: OP-003 names lineage, artifact, and evidence refs and family payloads but omits durable key shape, project scope, schema version, timestamps, causal/revision fields, actor identity, idempotency, and unknown-field compatibility rules.
items.impact: Independent producers and consumers cannot serialize, migrate, order, or deduplicate the supposedly shared envelope consistently.

evidence.exact_quote: Governance and runtime records use a shared record envelope with family-specific payload blocks so records remain distinct from artifacts, receipts, and rendered summaries.

items.title: Minimum concern record cannot persist the full lifecycle contract
items.statement: The required minimum shape omits resolution_kind, transition rationale, resolver authority, resolved/dismissed timestamp, prior-state/revision, and transition receipt even though those are mandatory lifecycle semantics elsewhere in the same owner section.
items.impact: A conforming minimum record can reach resolved or dismissed without enough data to audit, reopen, or distinguish accepted risk from a presentation dismissal.

evidence.exact_quote:
- It carries `resolution_kind`, including `accepted_risk`, together with a concern-action confirmation matrix for acknowledge, dismiss, resolve, and lineage-edit operations.
- The concern lifecycle transition matrix is owner prose here: `active -> acknowledged` records operator awareness without changing truth, `active | acknowledged -> resolved` requires evidence that the underlying issue changed, `active | acknowledged -> dismissed` requires a rationale that the concern presentation is intentionally hidden or rejected as actionable framing, and `resolved | dismissed -> active` is the reopen path when new evidence invalidates the prior resolution or dismissal. Resolved and dismissed guard rules require current projection data or direct record revalidation before mutation, and every transition persists through `concern_record` plus `concern_projection` linkage rather than a page-local status flag.

- Required fields: `concern_id`, `project_id`, `run_ref`, `scope_ref`, `source_event_ref`, `evidence_refs[]`, `artifact_refs[]`, `lineage_refs[]`, `severity`, `category`, `status`, `visibility_level`, `attention_level`, `chatworthy`, `blocking_effect?`.

items.title: Container-host access projections omit secret and lifetime controls
items.statement: OP-028 allows access URL pivots and sensitive host assignment information but does not specify URL expiry, one-time-token handling, credential redaction, audience, permission recheck, copy/log policy, or behavior after assignment termination.
items.impact: A stale or overexposed host URL can outlive its assignment or reveal credentials and infrastructure details to an unauthorized viewer.

evidence.exact_quote:
Orchestrator surfaces containerized-host readiness, assignment, blocker, access, and receipt projections for runs and
  attempts that use host capability, while Docker Manager, Docker/Hosts, Executor, Run Modes, ATS, Permissions, FileSafe,
  Tools, and Runtime Artifacts retain their owner roles. Orchestrator may show host readiness chips, blocked-action
  payloads, active assignments, access URL pivots, receipt/evidence links, and Docker/Hosts routes from run details, but
  it does not own local Docker, Kubernetes, SSH, shell, file, or cleanup mutation semantics and does not create a new
  top-level Orchestrator tab for Hosts. Stale projections cannot authorize sensitive actions; all mutation or launch
  requests resolve through HostCapabilityCommand and owner receipts.

items.title: Concern action metadata lacks execution semantics
items.statement: OP-005 requires authority, confirmation, rationale, reversibility, and audit fields but does not define command IDs, payload/result schemas, idempotency, optimistic concurrency, receipt persistence, or rollback behavior for each action family.
items.impact: Two implementations can expose the same labels while performing materially different or unsafe mutations, especially dismiss, resolve, merge, and split.

evidence.exact_quote:
- Acknowledge, dismiss, resolve, and structural lineage edits remain distinct actions.
  - Full record inspection routes to canonical records instead of expanding giant inline records.
  - User-facing actions remain narrow and true HITL approvals stay separate from generic runtime actions.

items.title: Direct revalidation is vulnerable to a validation-to-mutation race
items.statement: OP-006 allows mutation after direct revalidation but requires no source generation/revision token to be bound atomically to the command. last_observed_at and source_event_ref alone do not prevent the owner from changing after validation and before mutation.
items.impact: A projection can be revalidated, become stale immediately, and still authorize a destructive action against a changed target.

evidence.exact_quote:
- Mutation-capable projections carry projection_state, last_observed_at, source_event_ref, and revalidation_route.
  - Stale, degraded, and unavailable projections disable mutation unless the owner surface performs direct revalidation.
  - Wait and timeout cards show canonical retained timeout_class and route recovery through stored blocked episodes or receipts.

items.title: Object-first routes retain focused-run identity
items.statement: OP-007 explicitly carries stable object identity, focused run context, destination, filters, and inspector detail and forbids highlight-only routing and cross-run name collapse.
items.impact: Search and deep links have enough declared context to avoid silently switching from a historical run to the active run.

evidence.exact_quote: Search, command-palette, drill-down, and cross-tab deep links route by stable object identity, focused run context, destination tab, selected object id, optional filters, and inspector detail targets.

items.title: Notification escalation has no dedupe, rate, or delivery-state contract
items.statement: OP-008 names routing inputs and surfaces but does not define event deduplication, reminder cadence, burst/rate limits, delivery acknowledgement, timezone quiet windows, failed-delivery fallback, or mapping among its several alert vocabularies.
items.impact: The same concern can spam multiple surfaces, disappear after failed delivery, or render inconsistent severity labels.

evidence.exact_quote: Notifications, attention rows, blocked-owner summaries, escalation levels, quieting behavior, and surface routing are determined by severity, execution impact, blocked owner, persistence, and projection trust.

items.title: Durable account-pressure history has no privacy lifecycle
items.statement: OP-009 makes account pressure and switch events durable and project-scoped but supplies no retention, deletion, export, redaction, access-control, or account-identifier pseudonymization policy.
items.impact: Concrete provider-account identities and pressure histories can persist indefinitely or leak across users with project access.

items.title: Promotion decisions lack atomic version and falsifiable gate definitions
items.statement: OP-010 lists promotion classes and retained facts but does not define per-class required evidence sets, state transitions, concurrent approve/revoke precedence, version matching, or executable pass/fail fixtures.
items.impact: A stale approval can race a revocation or missing evidence can be treated as a passing generic promotion state.

evidence.exact_quote: Promotion classes, review records, gate facts, evidence expectations, decision outcomes, and revocation or reopen lineage remain explicit package, seam, lane, and governance data.

items.title: Progress widget catalog has no accessibility or localization contract
items.statement: OP-011 preserves thirteen widgets and fixed labels/taxonomies but gives no keyboard order, focus restoration, screen-reader names, live-region policy, non-color status cues, reduced-motion behavior, text expansion, or localization key strategy.
items.impact: A catalog-complete implementation may still be unusable with assistive technology or break under translated labels and text scaling.

items.title: Indeterminate remote outcomes do not define retry idempotency
items.statement: OP-012 preserves indeterminate outcomes and terminal precedence but omits remote operation idempotency keys, reconciliation ownership, polling/backoff ceiling, duplicate suppression, and the condition under which retry becomes safe.
items.impact: Retry after transport loss can duplicate a publish, rollout, or other external side effect before reconciliation determines the original result.

evidence.exact_quote: Artifact routing, external receipts, blocked cards, mutable target ownership, terminal-state precedence, and domain blocked payloads route to owner surfaces with retained lineage and explicit missing-link states.

items.title: Owner-surface navigation does not mint local mutation authority
items.statement: OP-013 clearly restricts Orchestrator commands to route-open pivots and sends recovery mutations through ordered runtime-owned actions.
items.impact: Source Control, Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, evidence, and artifact mutations retain their canonical owners.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator command exposure for recovery and navigation is route-open only into owner surfaces, while runtime mutation recovery maps through ordered allowed_action_ids to cmd.runtime commands.

items.title: Owner routes omit mandatory project scope and target-side authorization
items.statement: OP-013 says route fields are carried where available but does not require project_id, owner-surface object type/version, return route, or authorization recheck after restart. Optional identity fields can produce a valid-looking route to the wrong project or stale object.
items.impact: Deep links may disclose or act on an object outside the intended project, particularly after restart or identity reuse.

items.title: Debug resume revalidation is not bound atomically to resume
items.statement: OP-014 checks session and remote identities but supplies no generation token, lease, atomic compare-and-resume command, or handling for a target that disconnects or is rebound between validation and resume.
items.impact: Execution can resume against a different or no-longer-authorized debug target despite a successful prior revalidation.

items.title: SCM lineage display has no path and repository redaction policy
items.statement: OP-015 requires exact worktree, affected-file, repo, branch, and head lineage but does not say how sensitive local paths, repository names, branch names, or filenames are permission-filtered in shared UI, notifications, screenshots, or exports.
items.impact: Operational diagnostics can leak local machine structure or private repository details beyond the audience allowed to mutate the worktree.

items.title: Reconciliation-readiness classification has no completion oracle
items.statement: OP-016 defines an ordering and three buckets but no responsible adjudicator, evidence required for a bucket, machine-readable disposition, or terminal criterion for deciding owner and consumer corrections are complete enough to rerun fidelity.
items.impact: The same unresolved issue can be labeled cleanup by one builder and a structural gap by another, enabling false closure.

items.title: Help governance omits localization, accessibility, and version skew
items.statement: OP-017 defines layers and entry fields but not localized term handling, screen-reader access, keyboard invocation, offline availability, content version binding, or what happens when help describes a newer/older runtime schema.
items.impact: Canonical terms can drift in translation or help can instruct an inaccessible or unavailable action that does not match the running version.

items.title: OP-018 names scale mechanisms without limits or consistency semantics
items.statement: The PlanUnit has no dataset ceiling, latency or memory target, slice ordering/cursor contract, update behavior while virtualized, selection retention, inspector cancellation, or load-error recovery.
items.impact: Dense tabs may drop selections, reorder rows, show stale inspectors, or exhaust memory while still claiming virtualization compliance.

items.title: Owner-consumer map delegates instead of enumerating consumers
items.statement: OP-019 says ownership follows ContractRefs and existing boundary notes, but the PlanUnit does not list the actual producers, consumers, required fields, propagation direction, or compatibility obligations that constitute the map.
items.impact: A referenced document can change or omit a seam without this owner document detecting which Orchestrator projection or command breaks.

items.title: Retired OP-001 bridge cannot override fine-grained units
items.statement: The migration bridge is explicitly retired, retains audit lineage only, and is barred from acting as implementation-ready coverage for the live units.
items.impact: Generated migration metadata cannot silently regain product authority over OP-002 through OP-019.

items.title: Owner-section hydration is not objectively testable
items.statement: OP-020 requires headings to be hydrated but supplies only a manual review and tab/ownership acceptance bullets; it does not map every marker heading to required PlanUnits, required prose fields, or a completeness validator.

items.title: GoalRun and WorkNode projected statuses have no transition or aggregation matrix
items.statement: OP-022 lists eleven statuses for two object families without saying which statuses apply to which family, legal transitions, parent aggregation from WorkNodes, precedence among blocked/failed/cancelled/stopped, or behavior when verification and cancellation race.

items.title: Plan Compile stages and ETA have no semantic or accuracy contract
items.statement: OP-023 names current_stage, timeline, throughput, speed, ETA confidence, blockers, warnings, and readiness but defines no stage enum/state machine, denominator for progress, stalled/paused/cancelled behavior, confidence calculation, update cadence, or acceptable error.
items.impact: The tab can show precise-looking percentages and ETAs that are incomparable across stages or misleading during retries and parallel work.

items.title: History actions have labels but no command and receipt contracts
items.statement: OP-027 enumerates open, compare, duplicate, reopen, export, send-forward, resume, retry, clone, and rebuild behavior without command IDs, payload/result schemas, idempotency, authorization snapshots, confirmation levels, disabled-reason enums, or receipt effects.
items.impact: Resume, retry, clone, duplicate, rebuild, and send-forward can acquire inconsistent identities or mutate authority-bearing state without auditable semantics.

evidence.exact_quote:
canonical_text: History rows expose authority-gated actions without mutating immutable history in place. Document
  rows support Open, Compare versions, Duplicate as draft, Reopen in Wizard, Export, and Send forward when currentness
  allows; run rows support viewing, filtering, artifact/evidence opening, resume/retry where valid, clone-as-new-run,
  export, and raw/ledger inspection. Compare versions is deep in MVP with rendered output, package/source-lineage
  metadata, source ledger atom lineage where applicable, and manifest identity. Export actions support selected
  rows, multi-select bundles, filtered views, zip/archive, JSON, rendered Markdown, rendered HTML, rendered PDF,
  and explicit evidence/redaction profiles. When projection state is stale, compare/export/reopen/send-forward remain

items.title: Rebuild has no atomicity, concurrency, or rollback algorithm
items.statement: Rebuild is a visible gate for four actions, but the specification does not define its immutable input snapshot, handling of events arriving during rebuild, temporary generation, atomic swap, failure cleanup, cancellation, version proof, or whether a successful rebuild can already be stale.
items.impact: A rebuild can lose new history, publish a mixed generation, or unlock actions against data that became stale during reconstruction.

items.title: Evidence export privacy requirements lack a concrete enforcement contract
items.statement: The source requires explicit profiles and omission manifests but gives no profile schema, secret classes, field-level policy, viewer/exporter distinction, encryption, archive integrity, size limit, cancellation cleanup, or test fixture for forbidden data.
items.impact: Zip, JSON, HTML, PDF, and evidence exports can leak provider credentials, account details, raw payloads, or removed material despite displaying a redaction option.

- Do not silently include raw records or evidence in ordinary exports.
- Do not export secrets, unauthorized provider/account details, or evidence outside the user's permissions.
- Do not omit a manifest of redactions/omissions when evidence export is requested.

items.title: Safe-point retry command conflicts with runtime mutation ownership
items.statement: The owner-routing PlanUnit says runtime mutation recovery maps to cmd.runtime commands, but the later repair addendum defines cmd.orchestrator.safe_point_retry as the retry action without explaining a route-only wrapper or superseding the earlier authority rule.
items.impact: The page may mint a panel-local runtime mutation, creating two command authorities and inconsistent permission/receipt behavior.

items.title: Usage drill-through has no safe fallback or raw-payload authorization rule
items.statement: OP-029 normalizes routes when usage_event_ref is present and preserves raw_payload_ref plus provider/account correlation, but does not define disabled/fallback behavior when the primary ref is absent or authorization/redaction when opening raw payload and sensitive provider details.
items.impact: A consumer may fall back to an ambiguous timestamp/run key or reveal raw billing/provider material to a viewer who can see the summary row but not the source record.

evidence.exact_quote: Orchestrator usage, cost, ledger, evidence, history, and receipt rows are consumers of UsageRecord projection packets. They display source_class, source_confidence, source_authority, settlement_status, cost_status, quota_state, projection_freshness, projection_health, hidden/background contribution, and dedupe/parent-child refs when usage appears in a row or detail panel. `View in Usage`, `Show in Usage`, and `Show in Ledger` actions route through object_kind = usage_event and object_id from usage_event_ref whenever present, preserving usage_record_id, provider_attempt_ref, attempt_id, node_id, tool_call_id, trace_ref, receipt refs, raw_payload_ref, artifact_id, run_id, and thread_id as correlation/context fields.

items.title: Usage parent-child attribution lacks cycle and double-count rules
items.statement: OP-029 requires parent/child drill-through but gives no acyclicity, dedupe-key, streaming partial-to-final replacement, adjustment/reversal, aggregation, or maximum-depth rule.
items.impact: Background/subagent costs can be counted twice, disappear during settlement updates, or create recursive drill-through and unbounded traversal.

evidence.exact_quote: - Hidden/background usage contribution is attributed through parent_usage_record_id or child usage refs rather than silently folded into parent-only totals.

synthesis.overall_assessment: The source is unusually strong on ownership boundaries, projection truth, object identity, compatibility aliases, blocked-state visibility, offline degradation, and compile-versus-execution separation. It is not yet implementation-deterministic in several high-risk areas: shared record schemas, race-safe revalidation, remote-side-effect idempotency, command payloads and receipts, measurable scale, History rebuild/export semantics, privacy for visible evidence and host/SCM/account data, accessibility/localization, and executable acceptance fixtures.
synthesis.unknown_unknowns: The largest unknown-unknown surface is the combination of asynchronous owner projections, external side effects, restart-stable routes, and stale-generation action gating. Without a common version/idempotency envelope, individually sensible rules can compose into duplicate mutations or truthful-looking but cross-generation UI state.
